description: Checks practical Excel skills: formulas, data cleaning, PivotTables, charts and checking the accuracy of results.

competencies.name: Formulas and functions
competencies.description: Uses SUM, SUMIF, VLOOKUP and cell references correctly.

competencies.name: Data cleaning
competencies.description: Prepares messy lists so they can be analysed.

competencies.name: PivotTables and summaries
competencies.description: Summarises large lists by group and keeps summaries up to date.

competencies.name: Charts and reporting
competencies.description: Chooses and formats charts that are easy to read.

competencies.name: Accuracy and checking
competencies.description: Checks results against the source before sharing them.

questions.text: Cells A2:A5 contain Paid, Unpaid, Paid, Paid. Cells B2:B5 contain 50000, 30000, 20000, 10000. What does =SUMIF(A2:A5,"Paid",B2:B5) return?
questions.explanation: SUMIF adds only the values in B where column A says Paid: 50000 + 20000 + 10000 = 80000.

questions.text: Admission numbers are in column A, names in B and fee balances in C (rows 2 to 100). You type an admission number in F2. Which formula returns that student's fee balance using an exact match?

options.text: =VLOOKUP(F2,A2:C100,3,FALSE)
=VLOOKUP(F2,$A$2:$C$100,3,TRUE)
=HLOOKUP(F2,A2:C100,3,FALSE)
=VLOOKUP(F2,A2:C100,4,FALSE)

questions.explanation: VLOOKUP with the last argument FALSE finds an exact match and column index 3 returns the balance in column C.

questions.text: In D2 you type =B2*C1, where C1 holds a commission rate. When you copy the formula down, D3 gives a wrong answer. Which formula in D2, copied down, will use C1 correctly in every row?

options.text: =ROUND($B2*C1,0)

questions.explanation: Dollar signs make C1 an absolute reference, so it does not move when the formula is copied down.

questions.text: Your list of student records has some students entered twice. Which Excel feature removes duplicate rows?

options.text: Home > Merge and Center
Data > Remove Duplicates
View > Freeze Panes
Insert > Header and Footer

questions.explanation: Data > Remove Duplicates deletes repeated rows based on the columns you choose.

questions.text: A column of parents' phone numbers has extra spaces and mixed formats, such as 0712345678 and 712345678. Which actions help to clean it? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use TRIM to remove extra spaces around the numbers
Sort the column from A to Z so the formats become equal
Use Find and Replace or a formula to give every number the same format
Delete every row where the number looks different
Format the column as Text so a leading zero is not dropped

questions.explanation: TRIM removes extra spaces, one common format makes numbers consistent, and Text format keeps a leading zero. Sorting does not change formats, and deleting rows loses data.

questions.text: You import fee amounts from the school system. The total from SUM is lower than expected, and some amounts are left-aligned with a small green triangle. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The worksheet has already run out of empty rows
Some amounts are stored as text, not numbers
The formula points to a different workbook that is closed
The file is too large for Excel to add up the numbers

questions.explanation: Numbers stored as text are ignored by SUM. Convert them to real numbers.

questions.text: What is a PivotTable mainly used for?

options.text: Summarising a list by group, such as fees per class
Locking cells so that nobody else can edit the data in them
Converting a whole worksheet into a PDF file to send by email
Checking the spelling in many worksheets at the same time

questions.explanation: A PivotTable quickly summarises large lists by group, such as total fees per class, without writing many formulas.

questions.text: Your manager has 5,000 payment rows and wants total fees collected for each class and each term. What is the best approach?

options.text: Filter each class and term one by one and add the totals on a calculator
Build a PivotTable with Class in rows, Term in columns and Amount in values
Sort the list by class and type the totals by hand under each group
Remove duplicates from the Class column and read the totals from there

questions.explanation: A PivotTable with Class in rows, Term in columns and Amount summed gives all totals in one step and can be updated.

questions.text: You added 200 new payment rows below the data used by an existing PivotTable, but the pivot does not show them. What should you do?

options.text: Wait, because PivotTables update automatically as you type new rows
Delete the old rows so that the pivot can read the new ones
Change the number format of the Amount column to Currency
Refresh the PivotTable and extend its source range to the new rows

questions.explanation: A PivotTable does not update by itself. Refresh it, and make sure its source range (or an Excel Table) includes the new rows.

questions.text: Which chart is best for showing how monthly fee collection changed over 12 months?

options.text: Pie chart with 12 slices
Doughnut chart
Line chart
Map chart

questions.explanation: A line chart shows change over time clearly. Pie and doughnut charts show parts of a whole, not trends.

questions.text: You are preparing a one-page chart for the head teacher. Which practices make the chart easier to understand? Select all that apply.

options.text: Give the chart a clear title and labelled axes
Remove clutter such as heavy gridlines and extra decoration
Use many bright colours and 3-D effects so it stands out
Sort categories in a logical order, such as largest to smallest
Put as many different charts as possible on one page

questions.explanation: Clear titles, labelled axes, less clutter and a logical order help readers. Bright 3-D effects and too many charts make reading harder.

questions.text: Your report total is TZS 48,500,000 but the school accounting system shows TZS 48,200,000 for the same period. What should you do first?

options.text: Find the cause of the TZS 300,000 difference, such as duplicates or gaps
Send the report anyway and say that the difference is small
Change the formula so that the total matches the accounting system
Round both totals to the nearest million so the gap disappears

questions.explanation: A difference means something is wrong, such as duplicates, missing rows or text values. Find the cause before sharing the report.

description: Checks ability to choose suitable charts, define useful KPIs, design clear dashboards, avoid misleading visuals and explain data to an audience.

competencies.name: Choosing the right chart
competencies.description: Matches the chart type to the question being answered.

competencies.name: KPIs and metrics
competencies.description: Defines clear, measurable indicators linked to goals.

competencies.name: Dashboard design
competencies.description: Builds dashboards that are simple and easy to scan.

competencies.name: Honest, non-misleading visuals
competencies.description: Presents data fairly without exaggerating or hiding facts.

competencies.name: Telling a story with data
competencies.description: Explains findings clearly to a non-technical audience.

questions.text: You want to compare the average exam score of five classes in one term. Which chart is most suitable?

options.text: Line chart joining the five classes
Bar chart with one bar per class
Pie chart with five slices
Scatter plot of class names

questions.explanation: A bar or column chart compares values across separate categories clearly.

questions.text: You want to see whether students who study more hours also tend to get higher scores. Which chart best shows this relationship?

options.text: Pie chart showing each student's hours
Line chart of average scores by month
Stacked area chart of scores by class
Scatter plot of hours against scores

questions.explanation: A scatter plot shows the relationship between two numeric measures, one point per student.

questions.text: A manager asks you to show the number of students in each of 12 subjects. Some names are long, such as Information and Computer Studies. Which is most readable?

options.text: 3-D pie chart with 12 slices
Radar chart with 12 points
Horizontal bars sorted by size
Line chart joining the subjects

questions.explanation: A horizontal bar chart gives space for long labels, and sorting makes comparison easy. A 12-slice pie is hard to read.

questions.text: What is a KPI (Key Performance Indicator)?

options.text: A measurable value that shows progress toward a goal
A colour scheme used for charts in management dashboards
A software licence that is needed for reporting tools
A special type of chart used only in finance reports and audits

questions.explanation: A KPI is a measurable value that shows how well you are achieving an important objective.

questions.text: A school wants to improve fee collection. Which is the best KPI to track?

options.text: Number of SMS reminders sent to parents each month of the term
Number of fee receipts printed by the office every week of term
Percentage of invoiced fees collected by the end of term
Number of staff working in the accounts office at the school

questions.explanation: A KPI should measure the outcome you want. The share of invoiced fees collected shows real progress. Reminders sent only measure activity.

questions.text: A school owner asks for a dashboard of what matters. Which of these are clearly defined KPIs? Select all that apply.

options.text: Overall school quality, as people feel it
Attendance rate = days present divided by total school days
Fee collection rate = fees paid divided by fees invoiced
Number of charts on the dashboard
Student-teacher ratio = number of students divided by number of teachers

questions.explanation: Good KPIs have a clear formula. Attendance rate, collection rate and student-teacher ratio are all measurable. "Overall school quality" and "number of charts" are not defined measures.

questions.text: Where should the most important figures be placed on a dashboard?

options.text: At the bottom, after all the detailed tables
At the top, where they are seen first
Hidden in a second tab to keep the page clean
Spread evenly so that nothing stands out

questions.explanation: People read from the top left first, so key summary numbers go there, with details below.

questions.text: The head teacher says your dashboard with 18 charts is confusing. What is the best response?

options.text: Keep the charts that answer key questions, and group them
Add more colours so that each chart stands out better
Make all the charts smaller so they fit on one screen
Add animations so that the page looks more modern

questions.explanation: Fewer, well-chosen charts that answer the main questions make a dashboard easy to use. More colour or decoration adds confusion.

questions.text: Which is the best use of colour in a chart?

options.text: Give every single bar a different bright colour
Use red for everything that is important
Change the colours on each page to keep readers interested
Use calm colours and highlight only the key bar

questions.explanation: Colour should have a purpose, for example to highlight the item that matters, and keep the same meaning throughout.

questions.text: A bar chart's vertical axis starts at 90 instead of 0, so a rise from 92 to 95 looks huge. Why is this misleading?

options.text: Bars must always be shown in different colours
Charts should never show numbers above 90 on an axis
It exaggerates a small change, as bar length no longer matches value
Axes must always be hidden in bar charts to be fair

questions.explanation: Bar length should match the value. A cut-off axis exaggerates small differences.

questions.text: Fee collection rose from 62% to 64%. Your manager asks you to make the chart show "big growth". What should you do?

options.text: Start the axis at 60 and do not mention that it was cut
Use 3-D bars so that the rise looks much larger
Show only the last two months and hide the earlier results
Show it honestly and call the rise a small improvement

questions.explanation: Present the data honestly, with a proper axis and context, and describe it as a small increase. Do not exaggerate.

questions.text: You must present survey results to a parents' committee that is not technical. What is the best way to do it?

options.text: Show all the raw data tables first and explain every column
Give the main finding first, one or two clear charts, then an action
Explain the formulas you used before showing any results
Use technical statistical terms to show your expertise

questions.explanation: Start with the main finding in plain words, support it with one or two clear charts and suggest an action.

description: Checks knowledge of planning campaigns, using SMS, WhatsApp, email and social media responsibly, SEO basics, audience targeting and measuring results.

competencies.name: Campaign planning and goals
competencies.description: Sets clear goals and plans campaigns around them.

competencies.name: Channels and permission
competencies.description: Uses SMS, WhatsApp, email and social media properly and respects consent.

competencies.name: SEO and social media
competencies.description: Understands search visibility and effective social media posting.

competencies.name: Audience targeting
competencies.description: Chooses and segments the right audience for each message.

competencies.name: Measurement and analytics
competencies.description: Uses results such as cost per enquiry to improve campaigns.

questions.text: What should you do first when planning a marketing campaign?

options.text: Design the logo and choose the colours
Decide the goal and who you want to reach
Buy advertising space on radio or online
Write the final social media posts for the month

questions.explanation: Without a clear goal and audience you cannot choose the right message, channel or budget.

questions.text: A new private school wants more admissions for January. Which campaign goal is clear and measurable?

options.text: Make the school more popular and well known online
Get as many likes and followers as possible on Facebook
Post something new on Facebook every single day of term
Get 60 admission enquiries by 15 December

questions.explanation: A SMART goal has a number, a channel and a deadline, so you can check if it was reached.

questions.text: Before you send marketing messages to people by SMS, WhatsApp or email, what should you have?

options.text: Their permission to contact them
A list bought from a stranger
A very short message
A new phone number for each message

questions.explanation: People should have agreed to receive your messages. Messages sent without permission annoy people and can damage trust.

questions.text: A parent replies "STOP, do not send me more messages" to your school's promotional SMS. What should you do?

options.text: Keep sending messages in case they change their mind later
Send one more message asking them why they decided to leave
Remove the number from the marketing list straight away
Switch to sending WhatsApp promotions to that parent instead

questions.explanation: Respect the request: remove the number from marketing lists promptly. Continuing can anger parents and breaks trust.

questions.text: What does SEO (Search Engine Optimisation) mean?

options.text: Paying Google to show your advert at the top of search results
Sending the same email to many people at exactly the same time
Creating a business account on several social media platforms
Improving a site so it ranks higher in free search results

questions.explanation: SEO is the work of improving a website so that it appears higher in unpaid (organic) search results.

questions.text: Which action helps a school website appear in local searches such as "primary school in Arusha"?

options.text: Repeat the word "school" hundreds of times on the page
Use clear page titles and list the school on Google Business Profile
Hide extra keywords in white text on a white background
Buy thousands of visitors from unknown websites online

questions.explanation: Clear titles and useful content with words people search for, plus a local business listing, help search engines understand the school.

questions.text: Your school's Facebook page has low engagement. Which actions are likely to help? Select all that apply.

options.text: Post real photos and short videos of school activities (with permission)
Buy thousands of followers so the page looks popular
Reply to comments and messages quickly
Test posting times when parents are most likely to be online
Post the same advert twenty times a day

questions.explanation: Real photos and videos, quick replies and posting when parents are online build engagement. Fake followers and posting the same ad many times do not.

questions.text: A tuition centre wants to advertise Form 4 revision classes on Facebook. Who should the advert target?

options.text: Everyone in the world, so that the advert gets the most views
Children under 13 years old in any region of the country
Parents and students near the centre who are interested in education
People chosen at random each day, whatever their interests

questions.explanation: Good targeting focuses on people likely to buy: parents and students in the area who are interested in education.

questions.text: You split your parent contacts into groups, such as nursery parents and secondary parents, so each group gets a suitable message. What is this called?

options.text: Spamming
Segmentation
Rebranding
Cold calling by phone

questions.explanation: Segmentation divides an audience into groups with similar needs so messages are more relevant.

questions.text: What does click-through rate (CTR) measure?

options.text: Clicks divided by the number of times the advert was shown
Money spent on the advert divided by the number of enquiries
Total followers divided by the number of posts made
Messages sent divided by the number of messages read

questions.explanation: CTR = clicks divided by impressions, showing how many people who saw the advert clicked it.

questions.text: Ad A cost TZS 100,000 and brought 50 enquiries. Ad B cost TZS 150,000 and brought 60 enquiries. Your goal is enquiries at the lowest cost. Where should extra budget go?

options.text: Ad B, because it brought more enquiries in total than Ad A
Ad A, at TZS 2,000 per enquiry against TZS 2,500
Split equally, because the costs are the same for both
Neither, because the results cannot be compared fairly

questions.explanation: Ad A costs TZS 2,000 per enquiry (100,000 / 50). Ad B costs TZS 2,500 (150,000 / 60). Ad A is cheaper per enquiry.

questions.text: Your campaign got 20,000 views but almost no enquiries. What does this most likely tell you?

options.text: The campaign was successful because views are the main goal
You should spend more money on the same advert
Nothing, because views and enquiries are not related
People saw it, but the message or call to action may be weak

questions.explanation: Views show reach, not results. Check the message, call to action, audience and how easy it is to enquire.

description: Checks ability to plan content, pick suitable platforms, manage community conversations, read analytics and handle reputation problems for an organisation.

competencies.name: Content planning and calendar
competencies.description: Plans a varied schedule of posts around key dates.

competencies.name: Platform choice
competencies.description: Chooses the right platform and feature for each purpose.

competencies.name: Community management
competencies.description: Responds to followers politely, quickly and safely.

competencies.name: Analytics
competencies.description: Reads metrics correctly to judge what works.

competencies.name: Crisis handling and reputation
competencies.description: Responds calmly and honestly to errors, rumours and complaints.

questions.text: What is a content calendar?

options.text: A list of public holidays in the whole country
A report of last month's followers and likes
A schedule of what to post, where and when
A design template for posters and social media banners

questions.explanation: A content calendar is a schedule showing what will be posted, on which platform and when.

questions.text: You manage a school's pages. Exams, a holiday and the admission season are coming in the next month. How should you plan?

options.text: Post only on the day when something actually happens
Plan next month's posts around those key dates
Copy what other schools posted at the same time last year
Wait for ideas and post whenever you feel inspired

questions.explanation: Planning ahead around key dates keeps posting regular and relevant. Last-minute posting leads to gaps and mistakes.

questions.text: Which items belong in a healthy content mix for a school's Facebook page? Select all that apply.

options.text: Student achievements and events (with parent permission)
Reminders about term dates and deadlines
Posts that criticise staff or other schools
Short learning tips for parents and students
"Register now" adverts only, every single day

questions.explanation: A mix of achievements, useful reminders and educational tips keeps followers interested. Posting only adverts or staff politics does not.

questions.text: Which platform is best known for professional networking and recruiting?

options.text: TikTok
Instagram
WhatsApp Status
LinkedIn

questions.explanation: LinkedIn is built for professional profiles, jobs and business networking.

questions.text: A school wants to share fun short videos of a student talent show to reach young people. Which is the best choice?

options.text: Short videos on TikTok or Instagram Reels
Long text posts on LinkedIn and company blogs
PDF newsletters sent by email to all parents
Photos of printed notices uploaded to Facebook

questions.explanation: Short vertical videos suit TikTok and Instagram Reels, where young people spend time.

questions.text: A school wants to send fee reminders to parents so that parents do not see each other's phone numbers. Which approach is best?

options.text: Post the reminder in a large WhatsApp group with all parents
Write the reminder in a Facebook comment
Send individual messages or use a broadcast list
Post the reminder as a WhatsApp Status only

questions.explanation: Individual messages or a broadcast list deliver the reminder privately. A large group shows all numbers to everyone.

questions.text: A parent comments on your school's Facebook post: "My son's result slip was wrong." How should you respond?

options.text: Delete the comment so others do not see it
Reply politely and ask to continue by private message
Ask the parent to stop complaining about the school online
Wait a week and see whether other people comment

questions.explanation: Reply quickly and politely in public to show you care, then move private details to a direct message or phone call.

questions.text: One follower keeps posting abusive language and insults to other parents on your page. What is the best action?

options.text: Answer the person using the same rude language they used
Delete every negative comment from every parent on the page
Ignore it, because abusive people usually stop on their own
Remove abusive comments, warn them, and block if it continues

questions.explanation: Follow clear page rules: hide or remove abusive comments, warn the person, and block if it continues. Keep a record. Honest complaints should not be deleted.

questions.text: Which metric counts how many different people saw your post?

options.text: Impressions
Followers
Reach
Shares

questions.explanation: Reach counts unique people. Impressions count total views, including repeat views by the same person.

questions.text: Post A had a reach of 10,000 and 50 reactions. Post B had a reach of 2,000 and 100 reactions. Using reactions divided by reach, which post had the higher engagement rate?

options.text: Post B, with 5% against 0.5%
Post A, with 0.5% against 5%
Both are equal because both have reactions
Post A, because its reach is larger

questions.explanation: Post A: 50 / 10,000 = 0.5%. Post B: 100 / 2,000 = 5%. Post B performed better.

questions.text: A false post says a pupil was seriously injured at your school. It is spreading on WhatsApp and Facebook. What is the best first step?

options.text: Delete all the comments and say nothing about it to anyone
Tell school leadership, confirm the facts, then prepare a statement
Post an angry denial straight away, before checking any facts
Wait quietly for the rumour to die down by itself

questions.explanation: Inform school leadership immediately and check the facts. Then give an approved, honest statement. Acting without facts can make it worse.

questions.text: Your school page published a wrong exam date. What is the best practice?

options.text: Quietly delete the post and hope that nobody saw the mistake
Blame the teacher who gave you the wrong date to protect yourself
Post a clear correction, apologise briefly and inform parents
Leave it, because parents will find the right date themselves

questions.explanation: Correct the mistake quickly, say so openly and make sure affected parents are informed. Hiding it damages trust.

description: Checks ability to write clearly for an audience, create effective headlines and calls to action, edit carefully, and avoid plagiarism and unchecked facts.

competencies.name: Audience and purpose
competencies.description: Writes for the reader with a clear goal.

competencies.name: Clarity and structure
competencies.description: Uses simple, well-organised writing.

competencies.name: Headlines and persuasion
competencies.description: Writes honest headlines and calls to action that work.

competencies.name: Editing and proofreading
competencies.description: Finds and corrects errors before publishing.

competencies.name: Originality and fact-checking
competencies.description: Uses original work and checks facts and sources.

questions.text: What should you think about before you start writing?

options.text: How many pages you will be able to fill with text
Who the readers are and what you want them to do
Which difficult words you can use to impress people
Which font will look the most professional on the page

questions.explanation: Good writing begins with knowing who will read it and what you want them to understand or do.

questions.text: You must write a fee-deadline notice for parents, and many of them read English as a second language. What is the best approach?

options.text: Use formal legal language so the notice sounds serious
Write one long paragraph that explains the whole fee policy
Add idioms and proverbs to make it interesting
Use short sentences with the date, the TZS amount and how to pay

questions.explanation: Short sentences, simple words and clear details (date, amount, how to pay) make the notice easy to act on.

questions.text: Which sentence is the clearest?

options.text: Parents should pay the fees before 30 November.
Fees are to be paid by parents, who should make sure payment happens before 30 November.
It is required that fees be settled by parents at a time prior to 30 November.
There is an expectation that payment of fees will take place before the 30 November date.

questions.explanation: Short, active sentences are easiest to understand. Long passive sentences hide who must act.

questions.text: You are drafting a school newsletter. Which practices improve clarity? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use long, complex words to sound professional
Keep paragraphs short, with one main idea each
Use headings and bullet points for lists of dates
Prefer active verbs, such as "The school will close"
Put the most important information at the very end

questions.explanation: One idea per paragraph, headings or bullets and active verbs all help readers. Long words and burying key information make reading harder.

questions.text: Which headline is the most specific and useful for parents?

options.text: Big news is coming from our school this month, so stay tuned!
You will not believe what happened at our school this week!
Admissions open for Standard One: apply by 30 November
Important school announcement for everybody in the community

questions.explanation: A good headline tells readers exactly what the news is and what to do.

questions.text: You are writing a short WhatsApp message to promote after-school Maths classes. Which version has a clear call to action?

options.text: To reserve a place, reply "YES" on WhatsApp before Friday.
Our Maths classes are very good and useful for every child.
We have many experienced teachers who love teaching.
We hope that you will consider our classes in the future.

questions.explanation: A call to action tells the reader exactly what to do and by when.

questions.text: Which sentence for a school advert is both persuasive and honest?

options.text: We guarantee an A grade for every single student
Our Form 4 pass rate rose from 70% to 78% in 2025
We are the best school in all of Africa, with no doubt
Other schools in town are failing their students

questions.explanation: Honest persuasion uses specific facts that can be proven. Guarantees, unproven "best" claims and attacks on others are misleading.

questions.text: What is a good way to find mistakes in your own writing?

options.text: Take a short break, then read it aloud slowly
Rely only on the spellchecker in your software
Read only the first paragraph and the last one
Publish it and let readers report errors

questions.explanation: Leaving the text for a while and reading it aloud and slowly helps you notice errors you missed before.

questions.text: Why is a spellchecker alone not enough?

options.text: It only works for text written in the Swahili language
It always removes correct words from the text you type
It cannot check any grammar mistakes at all in a text
It misses wrongly used real words and wrong facts

questions.explanation: Spellcheckers miss correctly spelled but wrong words, such as "there" for "their", and cannot check dates, names or numbers.

questions.text: A colleague asks you to edit a parents' notice with dates, amounts in TZS and a phone number. Which check is the most important before it is published?

options.text: Check that the headline is written in a bigger font size
Make sure the notice fills at least one whole page
Check dates, amounts and the phone number against the source
Add more adjectives to make it more attractive

questions.explanation: Wrong dates, amounts or phone numbers cause real problems. Check them against the official source.

questions.text: You find a perfect paragraph on another school's website and want to use it in your own blog post. What should you do?

options.text: Copy it exactly, because it is public on the internet
Copy it and change only a few of the words in it
Copy it and remove the other school's name from it
Write your own version, and credit them if you use their ideas

questions.explanation: Copying someone's work is plagiarism. Write in your own words, and credit or ask permission if you use their words or ideas.

questions.text: A blog draft says "Studies show 90% of students prefer online lessons" with no source. What should you do before using it?

options.text: Keep it, because it supports the argument
Find and check the source, or remove the number
Change it to 95% so it sounds more recent
Keep it, but add the word "maybe" before the number

questions.explanation: Statistics without a source may be false. Find the original reliable source, or do not use the number.

description: Checks understanding of layout, colour, typography, file formats and resolution, brand consistency, and preparing files for print and social media.

competencies.name: Layout and composition
competencies.description: Arranges elements so the main message is clear.

competencies.name: Colour and typography
competencies.description: Uses colour and fonts for readability and meaning.

competencies.name: File formats and resolution
competencies.description: Chooses suitable file types and image quality.

competencies.name: Brand consistency
competencies.description: Applies logos, colours and fonts correctly.

competencies.name: Preparing print and social media assets
competencies.description: Prepares files correctly for printers and online platforms.

questions.text: What does white space (empty space) do in a design?

options.text: It wastes space and should always be filled with more text
It makes the design easier to read and look organised
It makes the file size smaller every time the design is saved
It is only needed on designs that will be printed on paper

questions.explanation: White space gives the eye a rest and makes text and images easier to read and separate.

questions.text: A poster uses six fonts and eight colours, and the date is hard to find. What is the best fix?

options.text: Add a thick border so that the poster looks complete and neat
Make all the text the same size so that it looks balanced and fair
Make the date and title prominent and limit fonts and colours
Add more images to fill the remaining empty space on it

questions.explanation: A clear hierarchy, with the key message largest and fewer fonts and colours, helps readers find information quickly.

questions.text: Which combination is easiest to read for body text?

options.text: Dark navy text on a white background
Light yellow text on a white background
Light grey text on a white background
Red text on a green background

questions.explanation: Strong contrast between text and background makes reading easier, including for people with weak eyesight.

questions.text: Which are good typography practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use only one or two font families in a design
Make the text large enough to read on a phone screen
Write long paragraphs in all capital letters
Use a decorative script font for all body text
Keep alignment and line spacing consistent

questions.explanation: Few fonts, readable sizes and consistent alignment help readers. All capitals for long text and decorative fonts for body text reduce readability.

questions.text: Which colour mode is normally used for designs viewed on screens, such as Instagram posts?

options.text: CMYK
Grayscale only
Pantone only
RGB

questions.explanation: Screens create colour with light, so RGB is used. CMYK is the standard for professional printing.

questions.text: Which file format is best for a school logo that needs a transparent background on a website?

options.text: JPG
DOCX
PNG
MP3

questions.explanation: PNG supports transparency. JPG does not, so a logo would show a solid background.

questions.text: What is the main advantage of a vector file such as SVG or AI for a logo?

options.text: It always has the smallest possible file size of any format
It can be enlarged to any size without becoming blurry
It works only on social media sites and on websites, not print
It automatically fixes spelling mistakes in the text of the logo

questions.explanation: Vector files are made of shapes and paths, so they can be scaled to any size without losing quality.

questions.text: A printer says the 300 by 200 pixel logo you saved from Facebook looks blurry on a large banner. Why?

options.text: It is too small, so it looks pixelated when enlarged
The printer ink was the wrong colour for the large banner
The logo should have been saved as a Word file instead
Banners can only ever print logos that are in black and white

questions.explanation: A small raster image is stretched when enlarged, so it looks pixelated. Use a high-resolution or vector original.

questions.text: What is a brand guide (or brand guidelines)?

options.text: A list of competitors and their prices in the market
A schedule of social media posts for the month ahead
A manual for learning to use design software
A document with rules for logo, colours and fonts

questions.explanation: A brand guide sets rules for using the logo, colours and fonts so the organisation looks consistent everywhere.

questions.text: A teacher asks you to stretch the school logo to fit a banner space and change its colours to match a slide. What should you do?

options.text: Stretch it, because the banner space is more important
Keep its proportions and official colours, and change the layout
Recolour it to match the colours of each new design
Crop the edges of the logo so that it fits the space

questions.explanation: Never stretch or recolour a logo. Keep its proportions and official colours, and adjust the layout around it.

questions.competency: Preparing print and social media assets
questions.text: You designed an A4 flyer for printing. What should you send the printer for best results?

options.text: A screenshot of the design from your phone
A JPG that was compressed by sending it on WhatsApp
A print-ready PDF with sharp images, CMYK colour and bleed
A low-resolution PowerPoint file saved in RGB colours

questions.explanation: Print-ready files use high-resolution images, CMYK colour and bleed, which is extra design beyond the cut line so no white edges appear.

questions.competency: Preparing print and social media assets
questions.text: You must use one design for an Instagram post and a Facebook cover photo. What is the best approach?

options.text: Resize for each platform and keep key text away from the edges
Upload the same image to both and let the platform fix it
Stretch the image until it fills the whole space on each one
Make the file bigger so the platform fits it automatically

questions.explanation: Each platform has its own recommended sizes. Resize or crop each version and keep important text in the safe area, away from the edges.

description: Checks how well a candidate manages existing school customers: building relationships, renewals, upselling, handling escalations and planning account work.

competencies.name: Relationship building
competencies.description: Builds trust with school leaders and staff.

competencies.name: Renewals and retention
competencies.description: Keeps customers by showing value and handling renewal concerns.

competencies.name: Upselling and adding value
competencies.description: Recommends extra products only when they solve a real need.

competencies.name: Handling escalations
competencies.description: Responds calmly and honestly to complaints and problems.

competencies.name: Account planning and tracking
competencies.description: Prioritises accounts and keeps good records.

questions.text: What is the best way to build long-term trust with a school customer?

options.text: Contact them only when it is time to renew
Check in often, keep promises and reply quickly
Give them big discounts even when they do not ask
Avoid talking about problems so that they stay happy

questions.explanation: Trust grows when you stay in regular contact, keep promises and respond quickly, not only when you want something.

questions.text: The head teacher of one of your customer schools has been replaced by a new head. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until the renewal date to introduce yourself to them
Assume nothing will change and continue exactly as before
Arrange an early meeting to learn the new head's goals
Send the new head an invoice with the old terms attached

questions.explanation: A new decision-maker may not know the product or your history. Meet early to learn their priorities and show the value.

questions.text: When should you begin renewal discussions with a school customer?

options.text: On the day the contract expires
After the customer has stopped using the service
Only when the customer asks about it
Two to three months before the renewal date

questions.explanation: Starting well before expiry gives time to review results, solve problems and handle budget approvals.

questions.text: A school says it may not renew because few teachers use the system. What is the best response?

options.text: Ask why usage is low and offer training and support
Offer a big discount to them straight away to keep them
Tell them it is their own staff's fault for not learning it
Accept their decision and close the account quietly without asking

questions.explanation: Find out why usage is low. Training, support and data on benefits may fix the problem. A discount does not solve low usage.

questions.text: A school hesitates to renew because of budget pressure. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Show the value the school received, using real data
Discuss options within company policy, such as a smaller package or payment plan
Warn that their data will be deleted immediately if they do not renew
Ask who is involved in the budget decision and what they need
Promise new features that have not been approved

questions.explanation: Showing value with data, offering options within company policy and understanding who decides are professional steps. Threats and unapproved promises damage trust.

questions.text: Which is a good example of upselling to a school?

options.text: Pushing the most expensive package to every school
Adding features the school never asked for to the invoice
Suggesting an extra module for a problem the school mentioned
Telling the school that competitors are worse

questions.explanation: Good upselling matches an extra product to a need the customer has already mentioned.

questions.text: A bursar tells you that parents often forget fee deadlines. Your company has an SMS reminder module. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until the bursar asks you directly about the reminder module
Explain how reminders solve this problem and offer a demo
Offer every available module at the same time in one big package
Quote the price only and say nothing about the benefits to them

questions.explanation: Link the extra module to the school's own problem and show how it helps, for example with a short demo.

questions.text: What does escalating a customer issue mean?

options.text: Passing it to a senior person, keeping the customer informed
Ignoring the issue until the customer stops complaining about it
Telling the customer to go and contact somebody else in the company
Closing the ticket without checking whether the problem is fixed

questions.explanation: Escalation means passing the problem to someone with more authority or specialist skill while keeping the customer informed.

questions.text: A bursar phones, angry that reports are not working before a board meeting. What is the best first response?

options.text: Say that this is not really the job of your department
Ask the bursar to call back again tomorrow when calm
Explain that other schools are not having this problem
Listen, then involve technical staff and give a time

questions.explanation: Listen, show you understand the urgency, confirm details, give a clear time and involve the technical team. Blaming or delaying makes it worse.

questions.text: You promised a school that a problem would be fixed by Friday, but the technical team says it will take until Monday. What should you do?

options.text: Say nothing and hope that it is fixed on time after all
Tell them on Friday afternoon when the time has passed
Tell the school before Friday, give a new date and a workaround
Blame the technical team for the delay in your message

questions.explanation: Tell the customer before the deadline, explain honestly, give a new date and offer a workaround if there is one.

questions.text: Which information belongs in your account notes for a school customer?

options.text: The login passwords of the school staff, bursar and head teacher
Key contacts, renewal date, past issues and actions
Personal gossip about the school staff members and their families
Your own opinion of the school's teachers and how they teach

questions.explanation: Good notes help colleagues continue the relationship: key contacts, renewal date, past issues and agreed actions. Passwords should never be stored.

questions.text: You manage 25 school accounts, some large, some small and some at risk. What is the best way to prioritise your time?

options.text: Spend exactly equal time on every school account
Help the school that complains most loudly first
Visit only the newest customers to help them settle
Give more time to large, at-risk or soon-to-renew accounts

questions.explanation: Focus on accounts that are large, at risk or close to renewal, while still keeping contact with all accounts.
